decisions.reason: As a low-cost finish variant within the core drainage range, it remains worth keeping because surviving another year would suggest usable demand while the option value of offering the colour line is still positive.

This shower channel is very close to the firm’s established architectural drainage business, so with no clear negative signal it is rational to continue it as a now less-uncertain extension of the core offer.

Although pump-assisted drainage is more complex and support-intensive, it still opens attractive niche applications for difficult installations, so the firm would likely keep the option open unless clearly weak sales emerge.
A tileable floor drain fits the firm’s barrier-free and design-led positioning closely, and the cost of maintaining such a core-adjacent product is likely too small to justify withdrawal.
As a complementary design grate with modest technical risk and likely low carrying cost, it makes sense to retain it while it continues to broaden the firm’s aesthetic range.

Because this pump-drain shower channel was only launched in 2024 and extends the core offer into more demanding use cases, management would likely give it more time rather than close the option early.
